title: Observability dependency rationalization and sampling/latency optimizations
creator: Maya Chen
description:
Background: Our current observability stack mixes legacy tracing hooks, two competing metrics libs, and an aging OTLP exporter that exhibits high allocations under sustained traffic. This ticket consolidates deps, updates OpenTelemetry, and implements targeted perf fixes so that trace latency and metrics emitter cost are reduced without changing user-facing telemetry semantics.

Goals: 
- Upgrade OpenTelemetry to the latest stable release that has the new batching/exporter internals and semantic-conventions alignment.
- Replace deprecated in-house metrics shim with the lightweight prometheus-adapter and a small compatibility layer to avoid churn across services.
- Move trace exporters to OTLP/gRPC with an async bounded queue and backpressure policy; keep Jaeger/Console for local dev only.
- Implement adaptive sampling (initial sample-rate 5%) with an emergency drop policy for extremely high throughput paths.
- Reduce allocations in the tracer hot-path by lazy-initializing span attributes and reusing buffers for common tags.
- Add rollout plan with canary, observability dashboards to validate regressions, and a rollback path.

Scope (what we will change):
- Service bootstrap logic: lazy tracer initialization and exporter config parsing moved off hot-path.
- Tracing instrumentation: replace legacy TraceHelper with OtelTracerAdapter (small shim).
- Metrics: remove metrics-v1 and wire prometheus-adapter behind MetricsShim for backward compatibility.
- Observability infra: upgrade otel-sdk, otel-exporter-otlp, and otel-semconv packages.
- Runtime performance: micro-optimizations in span allocation and attribute formatting.

Out of scope: migrating our storage backends (tempo/jaeger storage) or changing log formats in this ticket.
acceptance_criteria: All services compile and pass CI with new OTEL deps
No increase in 95th/99th percentile request latency after canary rollout (<= 1% delta relative to baseline)
Tracing CPU and heap allocations reduced at least 30% in the hot-path benchmark
Metrics scrape rates preserved and dashboard metrics remain stable (no missing labels)
Rollback documented and execute-able via feature flag within 15 minutes
